result.text: A guest enters the restaurant when feeling hungry.
He chooses a dish from the changing meal range and waits until it is his turn.
Following this he places his order with the employee.
The employee enters the order into the POS system and collects the money from the guest.

Afterwards the employee informs the chef of the new meal order.
The chef prepares the meal and places it in the service hatch.
He then informs the employee that he has placed the finished meal in the service hatch.
As soon as the employee is aware that the meal is ready he sets off the guest's buzzer.
This is how the guest finds out that his meal is ready for collection.
He can pick up his meal and eat it.
As soon as the guest appears at the service hatch, the employee hands over his meal.
Should a guest not react to the buzzer, the employee calls for him after 5 minutes, if necessary several times in a row.

result.rule: Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.
Direct each message flow from sender to receiver. Its endpoints must belong to different pools and be valid interaction nodes.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.

result.rule: When the description describes distinct participants communicating or exchanging an item, with an action by each participant: Model each described exchange as a message flow from the sending interaction node to the receiving interaction node in separate participant pools; represent distinct exchanges separately rather than combining them into one interaction.

When the description states that a participant submits information and that it is subsequently entered into a record or system.: Model submission and recording as distinct activities connected in the stated order.

When the description mentions sending information to, or receiving a response, payment, or other input from, an external party but describes no process work performed by that party: Model the described work and any necessary communication or waiting within the in-scope process; do not add a separate participant pool or message flows solely because the external party is mentioned.
